gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that the Lofree Flow 2's VIA remapping still needed a JSON definition file loaded by hand (Philipp Briel, basic-tutorials, 2026-03-31) and cannot remap the touch strip, or that the NuPhy Air75 V3 drops to 125 Hz on Bluetooth (João Silva, KitGuru).
standout_why: I compared against the three rival pages that returned a body: mechkeyfoundry.com/best-low-profile-mechanical-keyboard-wireless (cited), mechkeyfoundry.com/nuphy-air75-v3-vs-lofree-flow-2-vs-keychron-k3-max and the keeb-finder K3 Max vs Air75 V2 compare. mechkeyfoundry already gives the core compatibility matrix: K3 Max runs QMK and remaps in the browser through Keychron Launcher, Air75 V3 uses NuPhyIO rather than QMK or VIA, Flow 2 is VIA, Logitech MX Mechanical Mini has neither, and none of the sockets take MX switches. Those pages lack the Flow 2 JSON sideload step, the touch-strip exclusion, any Linux statement for any board, and per-mode polling rates. The cited RTINGS pages returned only navigation, so I could not check whether RTINGS already covers these points. The additions come from named reviewers, not from a maker document.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. The Keychron K3 Max stays the remapping-first choice (QMK through a browser, per mechkeyfoundry). Our Lofree Flow 2 84 honestly holds the premium-typing segment and is remappable through VIA on Linux, macOS and Windows (Notebookcheck), with a caveat the page should state: as of Briel's March 2026 review, VIA needed a JSON file loaded by hand and could not remap the touch strip. The Air75 V3 is the one of the three that is neither QMK nor VIA.

findings.label: Remapping software, maker statement
findings.value: "Flow 2 is fully compatible with VIA": remap any key, create macros, shortcuts and key combinations
findings.note: Maker page. It states no cable requirement, browser, operating system or JSON step for VIA.

findings.label: Connection modes and battery, maker statement
findings.value: 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth 5.3 and wired USB-C; 3,000 mAh in the 84-key Flow 2 against 2,000 mAh in the original Flow 84
findings.note: The page lists no polling rate per mode.

findings.label: VIA setup limit (named reviewer)
findings.value: Philipp Briel (basic-tutorials) wrote that "a JSON file is currently still required" to use VIA, and that the touch strip cannot be reconfigured through VIA
findings.source_title: LOFREE Flow2 Review: High-quality low-profile keyboard with German layout
findings.note: Review dated 2026-03-31, German-layout unit. Briel hoped the JSON step would go away; I could not check Lofree's download page today for whether it has. The review does not say which connection mode the VIA test used.

findings.label: Operating systems that can remap (named reviewer)
findings.value: Julian van der Merwe (Notebookcheck) wrote that "users on Linux, macOS, and Windows will all be able to remap the Flow 2" through VIA
findings.source_title: Lofree Flow 2: New wireless low-profile mechanical keyboard packs touch bar, new keycaps, and improved customisation with VIA
findings.note: Launch news dated 2025-06-13, not a hands-on test. Briel's review separately says Linux users get "full compatibility".

findings.label: Hot-swap and 2.4 GHz activation (named reviewer)
findings.value: Philipp Briel: switches are hot-swappable; 2.4 GHz mode must first be activated with FN+4; 1,000 Hz polling on 2.4 GHz
findings.source_title: LOFREE Flow2 Review: High-quality low-profile keyboard with German layout
findings.note: The review does not say which third-party switches fit the sockets.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection mode (named reviewer, quoting launch specs)
findings.value: 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz and USB-C; 125 Hz on Bluetooth 5.0
findings.source_title: NuPhy updates the Air75 for 2025 (KitGuru, João Silva)
findings.note: Launch article dated 2025-06-13. It also gives a 4,000 mAh battery, hot-swappable low-profile switches (Nano Red, Brown, Blush) and a $139.95 launch price. Its compatibility sentence lists Windows, Linux, Android and iOS.

findings.label: Remapping software (rival page)
findings.value: Uses NuPhy's own NuPhyIO configurator rather than QMK or VIA; takes Gateron low-profile 3.0 switches with hot-swap; ships in Mac and Windows layouts
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V3 vs Lofree Flow 2 vs Keychron K3 Max (MechKey Foundry)
findings.note: Rival page dated 2026-10-17; its author says they had not tested the NuPhy or Lofree boards. The switch and layout details are from its sister page, https://mechkeyfoundry.com/best-low-profile-mechanical-keyboard-wireless/. Neither page mentions Linux for any board.

findings.label: Remapping software and switch fit (rival page)
findings.value: Runs QMK and remaps through Keychron Launcher in a browser; hot-swap is on the RGB model only; the socket takes low-profile mechanical switches, not standard MX
findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboard (Mac and PC) (MechKey Foundry)
findings.note: Rival page dated 2026-10-16, cited by ChatGPT. It lists 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth 5.1 and wired USB-C at 1,000 Hz, and a $109.99 price as of its own date, against the $87.49 ChatGPT showed. Keychron's own page returned only navigation today.

findings.label: Layout availability and battery (rival page)
findings.value: ISO layouts listed (UK, DE, Nordic, SW); 1,550 mAh battery; low-profile keycaps only
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V2 vs Keychron K3 Max: Battery and ISO (keeb-finder)
findings.note: Aggregator, not the maker. The same page lists the Air75 V2 (not the V3) as ANSI only with 4,000 mAh. It notes ISO stock varies by store and region.

findings.label: MX switches do not fit any of the three sockets (rival page)

findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboard (Mac and PC) (MechKey Foundry)
findings.note: Already on a cited rival page, so it is not new.

findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboard (Mac and PC) (MechKey Foundry)
